key_insight: A self-supervised graph transformer can infer spatial, single-cell–level interactions directly from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data, overcoming limited gene panels and without needing known ligand–receptor pairs.
problem_solved: Existing methods for detecting cell–cell interactions rely on large gene panels or curated ligand–receptor lists, which are unavailable or incomplete in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics—this method infers interactions despite those limitations.
method: Build a spatial graph where nodes = imaged single cells and edges capture local neighborhood relationships.
Train a graph transformer with self-supervised objectives to learn cell representations and interaction scores from spatial and limited-expression signals (no LR priors required).
Use learned attention/interaction outputs to identify and localize putative cell–cell interactions at single-cell resolution.
impact: Provides a generalizable, label-free approach for extracting interaction networks from sparse spatial transcriptomic data, enabling AI/ML practitioners to apply transformer-based graph models for biological discovery and downstream analyses without curated ligand–receptor annotations.
